stem_book: Passage Q.(i) to (v). For an ideal gas, three different paths A, (B + C) and (D + E) from an initial state P₁,V₁,T₁ to a final state P₂,V₂,T₁ are shown in the figure. Path A is a reversible isothermal expansion from P₁,V₁ to P₂,V₂. Path (B + C) is a reversible adiabatic expansion (B) from P₁,V₁,T₁ to P₃,V₂,T₂ followed by reversible heating at constant volume (C) from P₃,V₂,T₂ to P₂,V₂,T₁. Path (D + E) is a reversible expansion at constant pressure P₁ (D) from P₁,V₁,T₁ to P₁,V₂,T₃ followed by reversible cooling at constant volume V₂ (E) from P₁,V₂,T₃ to P₂,V₂,T₁. (i) What is q_rev for path A? (a) P(V₂ − V₁) (b) −nRT₁ ln(V₂/V₁) (c) −nR ln(V₂/V₁) (d) −nRT₁ ln(V₂/V₁). (ii) What is q_rev for path (B + C)? (a) nR ln(V₂/V₁) (b) −nR ln(V₂/V₁) (c) zero (d) nRT₁ ln(V₂/V₁). (iii) What is ΔS for path A? (a) nR ln(V₂/V₁) (b) P(V₂ − V₁) (c) −P(V₂ − V₁) (d) nR(V₂ − V₁). (iv) What is q_rev for path (D + E)? (a) P(V₂ − V₁) (b) ∫_{T₃}^{T₁} C_V(T)/T dT (c) nR ln(V₂/V₁) (d) ∫_{T₁}^{T₃} C_V(T) dT. (v) What is ΔS for path (D + E)? (a) −P(V₂ − V₁) (b) −nR ln(V₂/V₁) (c) +P(V₂ − V₁) (d) nR ln(V₂/V₁)
